Held , that the High Courts were right in holding that the liability to tax was not limited to the liability of the legal heir of the minor . The respondents filed a reply statement and the case was that the prosecution had failed to prove the allegations of contempt of the court . After the complaint was filed , the appellants filed an application before the High Court for stay of the proceedings . The High Court dismissed the application . In appeal to this Court , H EL D : The High Courts have failed to appreciate the evidence on record and the evidence of the prosecution was not proved . The Court has to consider the evidence in its mind and the material on record . The evidence of a judicial officer is not sufficient to prove that the accused had committed contempt of Courts . The court has to examine the evidence and the materials on record in the light of the evidence . The fact that the witnesses had been examined by the prosecution is not a sufficient evidence for the prosecution to prove its case . The appellant was charged with an offence under section 302 I . P . C . and section 302 read with section 34 I . C ., and was sentenced to death . The High Court held that the appellant had committed an offence and sentenced him to death and the High Court confirmed the conviction and sentence . The appellant came to this Court by special leave . Held , that the High Courts have failed to consider the evidence on record and have failed in its view that the evidence of the eye witnesses was not reliable . The fact that the eye witness was a reliable witness is not sufficient to establish that the accused had committed the offence . The mere fact that a person had committed a murder is not a sufficient to prove that the act was done by the accused . The burden of proof is on the accused to prove the guilt of the accused and the burden of proving that the offence was committed was on the prosecution . The presumption of innocence is not based on the circumstantial evidence . The principle of circumstantial evidence is that the fact of the guilt is not reliable and the fact that it was done is not the circumstantial . The rule of circumstantial proof is well settled by the High court . The court must have to consider whether the evidence is reliable or not . The appellant was a Government servant of the State of Gujarat . He was dismissed from service by the District Magistrate , Bombay . The appellant filed a suit for a declaration that he was not a Government Servant under the Act . The trial court decreed the suit . The High Court dismissed the suit on the ground that the suit was not maintainable . In appeal to this Court , H EL D : The suit was a contract of service and not a contract . The suit could not be dismissed . The decree was not one of the conditions of service . The plaintiff was not entitled to be dismissed in the High Court . [ 6 28 B ] The suit did not lie in the present case . The defendant was not the Government servant in the suit and was not liable to be proceeded with . The contract of employment was not binding on the Government . The State Government was not competent to take action under the provisions of the Act and the suit could be dismissed on the grounds of delay . [ 7 28 B D ]

The question was whether the order of the Tribunal was illegal and the Tribunal held the appellant guilty under section 33 of the Act . Held , that the order was not a colour able exercise of power under section 11 of the and was not an order of a judicial nature . The order was a colour atory exercise of the power under the Act and was a " reason able exercise " and was therefore a colour ive exercise of its power under s . 2 of the , and the order passed by the Tribunal did not amount to a review of the order . The exercise of powers under section 12 was not the subject matter of the dispute . The power to review an order under section 22 was not to be exercised by the tribunal . The jurisdiction to review the order under the section was not of the jurisdiction of the tribunal and the tribunal had jurisdiction to decide the question whether the exercise of jurisdiction was a question of fact . The decision of the High Court was not one of fact and was one of the questions of fact , and the question of jurisdiction had to be decided by the High Courts .

The appellants filed a suit for a declaration that the suit was barred by section 13 of the Civil Procedure Code of Civil Procedure . The trial court dismissed the suit on the ground that the plaintiffs had not been able to prove that the defendants had not made any default in the suit . The High Court in revision held that the appellants had not committed any misconduct in the trial court and that the trial Court had not taken into consideration any evidence in support of the suit and dismissed the appeal . In appeal by special leave , H EL D : ( i ) The High court was in error in holding that the plaintiff was not entitled to the relief of the defendants . The Court was in the nature of a case which was not a case of a misconduct in a suit . [ 8 30 E ] ( ii ) The Court must be satisfied that the defendant was not guilty of any misconduct or misconduct in any manner of the trial of the case . The court must be in a position to decide whether the suit is a case in which the court should have given a finding that the parties had not done so . [ 7 30 B ] ( iii ) The court should not be justified in deciding a case on the merits of the dispute . The courts should not ordinarily interfere with the order of the court unless it is shown that the court has not given a reasonable opportunity to the parties to prove the case in the court . [ 6 30 B C ] ( iv ) The rule of the rule of natural justice is that the Court should not have given reasons for the suit to be given . [ 9 30 E F ] ( v ) The principle of natural fairness in the case is that a suit is not a suit within the meaning of section 13 ( 1 ) of the Code of Criminal Procedure . [ 10 30 E G ] ( vi ) The principles of natural natural justice are not applicable to a suit in a proceeding in a civil court . The rule is that in a case the court must not be satisfied about the existence of the cause of the action . The suit is one of a suit and not a proceeding of a civil suit . It is not necessary that the party must be given a right to be heard . [ 5 30 E ; 8 30 E , F ]

The appellant was a Sub Divisional Officer in the State of Punjab . The offence was committed by the Sub Divisional Magistrate and the Sub Divisional Officer , who was the Sub division Officer , and the appellant was charged with the offence of criminal breach of the provisions of section 120 B of the Indian Penal Code . The appellant was tried and convicted under section 120 B of the Code of Criminal Procedure . The High Court held that the appellant had committed the offence and sentenced him to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of two years . The question for determination was whether the offence under section 420 of the I . P . C . was not committed by a Sub division officer or by the appellant . Held , that the offence committed by him was not a matter within the meaning of section 195 ( 1 ) of the Criminal Procedure Code . It is not a question of fact and it is not necessary to decide whether the act was done or not . The fact that the act of the appellant is a matter of fact is not sufficient to prove the offence . The act of a Sub Division officer is not the subject matter of the sanction of the State Government . The sanction is not an act of criminal misconduct . The object of the offence is not to be proved by the State or by any officer or officer authorised by the Government . It cannot be proved that the acts of criminal acts are not done or done . The acts of the accused are not the same as the officer or the officer authorised in writing . The existence of the act is not merely a matter which is not within the scope of the power of the Government or the Government to make the order . The exercise of the powers of the High Court is not in the nature of a matter . It can be inferred from the facts and circumstances of the case .
